reviews.title: DON’T BUY - Pay twice before you can even hear the result
reviews.text:
I really wanted to love this. I wanted to hear my own voice singing, and what I got sounded nothing like me.

First, the app asked for $9.99 to analyze my voice. I paid and spent around TEN MINUTES reading aloud. Once the analysis finished, there was no preview. Instead, I hit another paywall: $6.99 a week or a yearly subscription just to hear the result I had already paid to create.

I went ahead because I was excited to hear it. Had there been even a short preview, I would have stopped immediately and requested a refund.

I’m a woman with a fairly high voice. The generated voice sounded like a man trying to sound like a woman. It didn’t capture my pitch, my lisp, or anything that made it recognizable as me. After all that recording, how was the result this far off?

And there was no way I could find to fix or retrain that voice. The option was to create another one, which meant paying ANOTHER $9.99 for another voice license. Why would I pay again when the first attempt failed so badly?

The covers feature was also hugely disappointing. I only had three songs to choose from. The app lets you select favorite songs and genres, but I couldn’t actually cover those songs. Being able to hear myself sing familiar songs was the whole reason I downloaded it.

Charging for voice analysis, withholding the preview behind a subscription, and then charging again to try replacing an unusable result feels predatory. Let people hear a sample before asking for more money. My experience came n

⭐ 1/5

Very disappointing experience with Mozart AI. I originally found this service through social media advertising and signed up expecting to receive the service that was advertised. Unfortunately, the app did not work properly for me, and I was unable to get the service I believed I was paying for.

What concerned me even more was the billing process. After signing up through social media, I encountered charges involving third-party companies in addition to charges associated with the app. From my experience, it was not clear enough who was charging me, what each charge was for, or how the different companies were connected. I believe there needs to be much more transparency about third-party billing before customers provide payment information or subscribe.

I tried to cancel and made it clear that I no longer wanted the service, yet I was charged another $19.99. I have contacted Apple regarding the charges and requested a refund.

My biggest issue is not simply that the app didn’t work for me. It’s the lack of clarity surrounding the billing, the additional charges I encountered, and the difficulty I’ve had getting everything canceled and resolved.

Based on my experience, I strongly encourage anyone considering Mozart AI to carefully review exactly who is processing the payment, whether any third-party services are involved, what recurring charges they are agreeing to, and how cancellation works before signing up.

However, you first must pay a weekly monthly or yearly subscription, which basically gets you nothing. Then to use your voice, they charge you more money. To create a video which is not the length of the song, they charge you a lot more. And because it only gives you up to 60 seconds, they charge you even more to do 20 more seconds. Hopefully someone else picks up this model and charges less.

I’m determined now to make a comparison recording of what this app THINKS my voice is vs what it actually is. Was fun and silly to try once though. They won’t get more than the week subscription out of me though.

reviews.text:
This app is not as advertised. After paying for a subscription, I was surprised to find that additional charges are required at every step of the process. You have to pay to record your voice, and then pay again to merge your voice with a song.

If you’re already paying for a subscription, it’s unclear why basic functionality is locked behind extra fees. There are other platforms that offer the same features with a single subscription and no additional charges.

Overall, this was disappointing and not the value I expected, especially after already committing to a paid subscription

reviews.title: AI voice overlay is fuzzy no matter what mic is used
reviews.text: I just got the app to try for fun. Seemed easy to use, the interface is good and the processing is fast for covers. However, no matter what microphone is used (phone, headset, professional recording studio mic) the voice cover applied to songs using the voice within the app is fuzzy and over-uses auto tune. The music is bright and clear, but the cover voice sounds like it is coming from a tin can or transistor radio every single time. Even on a cappella songs. Not worth the money they charge at all. My guess is that the developers were pushed to release a product before it was completed. I plan to delete and push for the refund.

reviews.title: Scam
reviews.text:
They market the ability to use your voice and face to create a song that looks and feels like you are really singing. The marketing is impressive, so like most people you choose the cheapest plan to test the app and see if it is something you would commit to long term.

You then upload your photo and record a five minute voice sample, which takes time and effort. Here is the problem. Instead of being able to pick a song and generate the video you were promised, the app asks you to pay another $10 before anything can be created.

I cannot stand companies that are not transparent upfront. At that point I stopped the process and cancelled the app. The developer walks away with $7 and the consumer walks away with nothing. If your product is good, people will happily pay for it. There is no reason to rely on tricks and surprise fees to get more money.
